summary:
[  edit  ]
The Particle  SOP  is used for creating and controlling motion of "particles" for particle systems simulations. Particle systems are often used to create simulations of natural events such as rain and snow, or effects such as fireworks and sparks. In Touch, the points of the input geometry are used as the starting positions of the particles. Each point of the input can be affected by external force (gravity) and wind. Particles can collide and bounce off another object, set by the  Collision Source . They can also bounce off, or die at, limit planes set in X, Y and Z.
Particles are created with an initial velocity/direction that comes from the source geometry’s point normals, and that velocity can be controlled by modifying the normals using, for instance, a  Point SOP ,  Facet SOP  or  Script SOP . A point with a Normal of magnitude 1 emit bear particles with a velocity of 1 unit per second in the direction of the normal.
Particles have various  Attributes  that regular geometry do not have, such as velocity, life expectancy and age. These attributes must be carried with each point in order to carry out the simulation.
The fourth input is Surface Attractors that cause the particles to be attached to areas of a surface. Each particle's id is used to determine a random target primitive, and random u,v on that primitive.  That target position is used to modify the current velocity.

parameters.label: Particle Type
parameters.name: prtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Selects how the particles are rendered.

parameters.label: Render as Lines
parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: Each particle will be rendered as a 2-point line, with the length determined based on the particles velocity. If the particle has no velocity it will just be a single pixel in size.

parameters.label: Render as Point Sprites
parameters.name: pointprites
parameters.description: For use with the  Point Sprite MAT . Each particle is a square of pixels that always face the camera. The size of the square is determined by parameters in the Point Sprite and the  pscale  vertex/point attribute. The point sprites will have texture coordinates generated for them automatically also ((0,0) in the bottom left and (1,1) in the top right).

parameters.label: Behavior
parameters.name: behave
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select between emitting particles from the geometry's points or deforming the original geometry using the Particle  SOP 's behavior.

parameters.label: Particle System
parameters.name: psystem
parameters.description: Act like a particle system, where particles are born from the input points.

parameters.label: Modify Source  Geometry
parameters.name: modify
parameters.description: Deforms the source input geometry.

parameters.label: Compute Normals
parameters.name: normals
parameters.description: Creates normals on the geometry.  Only used when  Behaviour  is set to  Modify Source  Geometry  .

parameters.label: Point Reuse
parameters.name: ptreuse
parameters.description: ⊞  - Decide how the internal memory for points is reused when a point needs to be created or when a point dies.

parameters.label: Preroll Time
parameters.name: timepreroll
parameters.description: How many seconds of the simulation to bypass, after the reset time is reached. For example, if you put the number  33  into this field (and reset is at  Tstart ), frame one will show the simulation that was at a time of 33 seconds. In other words, the first thirty-two seconds have been bypassed, and the time at thirty-three seconds is shifted to frame one. The first thirty-two seconds must still be calculated in order to compute the status of the points, so you will notice some delay upon reset.

parameters.label: Time Inc
parameters.name: timeinc
parameters.description: The  Time Inc  parameter determines how often to cook the  SOP . By default, this parameter is set to   1  /  me  .  time  .  rate  . This means that the  SOP  will cook once for every frame. When complex dynamics are involved, the  SOP  may require more frequent cooking for increased mathematical accuracy. To get sub-frame accuracy in the cooking, set the  Time Inc  to something smaller than   1  /  me  .  time  .  rate  .

parameters.label: Max Steps
parameters.name: maxsteps
parameters.description: Limits how far back in time TouchDesigner calculates particle positions for proper interactions.  If frame rates are slow this computation back in time can become high, this parameter limits that effect.

parameters.label: Jitter Births
parameters.name: jitter
parameters.description: This allows you to jitter the location pixels of each particle as they are born.

parameters.label: Accurate Moves
parameters.name: accurate
parameters.description: This option makes the particles move more accurately between frames by calculating their trajectories for fractional frame values.

parameters.label: Remove Unused Points
parameters.name: rmunused
parameters.description: Removes all unused points from the input geometry. This is provided as an explicit option instead of automatically because it saves the time needed to purge the points from memory during the simulation. This prevents unnecessary slowdowns during the simulation.

parameters.label: Attractor Use
parameters.name: attractmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select which mode of attraction to use for Surface Attractors.

parameters.label: All Points
parameters.name: all
parameters.description: All point attractors affect all particles (or points).

parameters.label: Single Point per Particle
parameters.name: single
parameters.description: When enabled, each particle is assigned a single attractor point, and is affected by only that point. Assignment is done by point number modulo the total number of attractor points.

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: When On the particle system is held in a reset state and does not emit particles.

parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.description: Instantly reset the particle system to its starting state.

parameters.label: External Force
parameters.name: external
parameters.description: ⊞  - Forces of gravity acting on the particles. When drag is zero, the particles can accelerate with no limit on their speed.

parameters.label: Wind
parameters.name: wind
parameters.description: ⊞  - Wind forces acting on the particles. Similar to  External Force . Using  Wind  (and no other forces, such as  Turbulence ), the particles will not exceed the wind velocity.

parameters.label: Discussion
parameters.description: Wind vs External Force

parameters.label: Turbulence
parameters.name: turb
parameters.description: ⊞  - The amplitude of turbulent (chaotic) forces along each axis. Use positive values, if any.

parameters.label: Turb Period
parameters.name: period
parameters.description: A small period means that the turbulence varies quickly over a small area, while a larger value will cause points close to each other to be affected similarly.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Random number seed for the particle simulation.

parameters.label: Add Particle ID
parameters.name: doid
parameters.description: Adds an ID number to each particle as it is born.  Note:  New attributes only appear once the particle system is reset via the  reset  parameter or loads for first time.

parameters.label: Add Mass Attribute
parameters.name: domass
parameters.description: When selected, calculates the mass of the particle, as specified in the  Mass  field.

parameters.label: Mass
parameters.name: mass
parameters.description: The relative mass of each particle. Heavier particles take longer to start moving, and longer to slow down.

parameters.label: Add Drag Attribute
parameters.name: dodrag
parameters.description: When selected, calculates the drag coefficient of the particle, as entered in the  Drag  field.

parameters.label: Drag
parameters.name: drag
parameters.description: Drag of each particle.

parameters.label: Birth
parameters.name: birth
parameters.description: The number of particles born each second. Particles are not released in clusters. They are born at random times during the first frame of their existence. Their birth time is set randomly during the first frame.

parameters.label: Life Expect
parameters.name: life
parameters.description: How long each particle will exist, in seconds. The default is  3  seconds. You may want to adjust this number based on the length of your animation.

parameters.label: Life Variance
parameters.name: lifevar
parameters.description: Variance of a particle's life expectancy in seconds. If life expectancy is one second, and the variance is zero seconds, each particle will live exactly one second. If variance is set to 0.5, then some particles will live only a half second, while others will live a second and a half. The rest will live some time in-between. This randomness gives a more natural look to the particle births.

parameters.label: Alpha Speed
parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: As a particle goes faster, it should become more transparent. The  Alpha Speed  parameter defaults to 0, which doesn't change alpha as the speed increases. A typical value of 0.5 causes the particle to be 70% opaque when it's going 1 unit/second. Increasing the  Alpha Speed  parameter makes it more transparent at a given speed. At zero speed, a particle is always 100% opaque.

parameters.label: Surface Attraction
parameters.name: subattract
parameters.description: Gives control over how much particles are attracted towards the Particle  SOP 's 4th input surface attractor.

parameters.label: Birth Count
parameters.name: birthcount
parameters.description: Specifies the number of particles created when the Birth pulse parameter is hit.

parameters.label: Birth
parameters.name: birthpulse
parameters.description: Manually create n particles when pulsed. The number of particles created is controlled by the Birth Count parameter.

parameters.label: + Limit Plane
parameters.name: limitpos
parameters.description: ⊞  - The particles will die or bounce off the limit planes when it reaches them. The six limit plane fields define a bounding cube. The default settings are  1000  units away, which is very large. Reduce the values to about one to see the effect.

parameters.label: - Limit Plane
parameters.name: limitneg
parameters.description: ⊞  - The particles will die or bounce off the limit planes when it reaches them. The six limit plane fields define a bounding cube. The default settings are  1000  units away, which is very large. Reduce the values to about one to see the effect.

parameters.label: Hit Behavior
parameters.name: hit
parameters.description: ⊞  - Control over what happens when a particle hits either the six collision planes or the collide object. The options are:

parameters.label: Die on Contact
parameters.name: die
parameters.description: The particles will disappear when they collide with the Collision input.

parameters.label: Bounce on Contact
parameters.name: bounce
parameters.description: The particles will bounce upon contact with the Collision input.

parameters.label: Stick on Contact
parameters.name: stick
parameters.description: The particles will stick to the Collision input.

parameters.label: Gain Tangent
parameters.name: gaintan
parameters.description: Friction parameters which can be regarded as energy loss upon collision. The first parameter affects the energy loss (gain) perpendicular to the surface. 0 means all energy (velocity) is lost, 1 means no energy is lost perpendicular to surface. The second parameter is the energy gain tangent to the surface.

parameters.label: Gain Normal
parameters.name: gainnorm
parameters.description: Friction parameters which can be regarded as energy loss upon collision. The first parameter affects the energy loss (gain) perpendicular to the surface. 0 means all energy (velocity) is lost, 1 means no energy is lost perpendicular to surface. The second parameter is the energy gain tangent to the surface.

parameters.label: Split
parameters.name: splittype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select if the particle will split and under what conditions.

parameters.label: No Splitting
parameters.name: no
parameters.description: The default setting, this keeps the particles intact.

parameters.label: Split on Contact
parameters.name: bounce
parameters.description: The particles will split upon contact with the Collision Source.

parameters.label: Split on Death
parameters.name: die
parameters.description: The particles will split when they die.

parameters.label: Min/Max Splits
parameters.name: split
parameters.description: ⊞  - When a particle splits, it splits into a number of other particles. The number of particles is randomly set between this range.

parameters.label: Split Velocity
parameters.name: splitvel
parameters.description: ⊞  - Each split particle is given this base velocity.

parameters.label: Velocity Variance
parameters.name: splitvar
parameters.description: ⊞  - This is a random amount that is added to the split velocity. When creating fireworks, the variance is large while the velocity is low. When rendering raindrops splashing, the split velocity is large in Y, and the variance in X and Z causes the particles to bounce up - but randomly - in the XZ plane.

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.

Optimization**: References unchanged attributes, allocating memory only for modified data. - **Math Operations**: POPs like `Math`, `Transform`, and `Normalize` enable coding-free manipulations. - **Multi-Input Support**: POPs like `Merge` and `Switch` handle multiple inputs with flexible configurations. - **Swizzling**: Manipulate attribute components (e.g., `P.xy` for X and Y). ## 5. Practical Applications - **Rendering**: POPs drive 3D geometry with attributes like `Color` and `Normal`. - **Particles**: Points with attributes (e.g., `Vel`, `PartForce`) for simulations. - **Point Clouds**: Efficiently manage large datasets without TOPs’ 4-channel limitations. - **External Output**: Send data to lasers, DMX, or LEDs. ## 6.
